sanskrit: kaliṅgas tu maheṣvāsaḥ putraś cāsya mahārathaḥ śakradeva iti khyāto jaghnatuḥ pāṇḍavaṃ śaraiḥ
english: But the Kaliṅga king, a mighty archer, and his son, a great car-warrior renowned as Śakradeva, struck at the Pāṇḍava with their arrows.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahābāhur vidhunvan ruciraṃ dhanuḥ yodhayām āsa kāliṅgān svabāhubalam āśritaḥ
english: Then mighty-armed Bhīma, shaking his gleaming bow, gave battle to the Kāliṅgas, relying on the strength of his own arms.

sanskrit: śakradevas tu samare visṛjan sāyakān bahūn aśvāñ jaghāna samare bhīmasenasya sāyakaiḥ vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi tapānte jalado yathā
english: But Śakradeva, loosing many shafts in the fray, slew Bhīmasena's horses with his arrows, and rained down showers of arrows like a cloud at the end of the hot season.

sanskrit: hatāśve tu rathe tiṣṭhan bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ śakradevāya cikṣepa sarvaśaikyāyasīṃ gadām
english: But Bhīmasena of great might, standing upon his car whose horses were slain, hurled at Śakradeva a mace made wholly of refined iron.

sanskrit: sa tayā nihato rājan kaliṅgasya suto rathāt sadhvajaḥ saha sūtena jagāma dharaṇītalam
english: Struck down by it, O king, the son of the Kaliṅga king fell from his car, together with his banner and his charioteer, to the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: hatam ātmasutaṃ dṛṣṭvā kaliṅgānāṃ janādhipaḥ rathair anekasāhasrair bhimasyāvārayad diśaḥ
english: Seeing his own son slain, the lord of the Kaliṅgas hemmed in Bhīma on every side with many thousands of cars.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahābāhur gurvīṃ tyaktvā mahāgadām udbabarhātha nistriṃśaṃ cikīrṣuḥ karma dāruṇam
english: Then mighty-armed Bhīma, casting aside his heavy great mace, drew forth his sword, eager to perform a terrible deed.

sanskrit: carma cāpratimaṃ rājann ārṣabhaṃ puruṣarṣabha nakṣatrair ardhacandraiś ca śātakumbhamayaiś citam
english: And he took up, O king, O bull among men, a peerless shield of bull's hide, adorned with stars and half-moons wrought of gold.

sanskrit: kaliṅgas tu tataḥ kruddho dhanurjyām avamṛjya ha pragṛhya ca śaraṃ ghoram ekaṃ sarpaviṣopamam prāhiṇod bhīmasenāya vadhākāṅkṣī janeśvaraḥ
english: Then the Kaliṅga king, enraged, stroked his bowstring, and taking up one dreadful arrow like the venom of a serpent, the lord of men sent it forth at Bhīmasena, longing to slay him.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ vegena preritaṃ niśitaṃ śaram bhīmaseno dvidhā rājaṃś ciccheda vipulāsinā udakrośac ca saṃhṛṣṭas trāsayāno varūthinīm
english: That sharp arrow speeding swiftly upon him, Bhīmasena cut in two, O king, with his broad sword, and shouted aloud in his joy, striking terror into the host.

sanskrit: kaliṅgas tu tataḥ kruddho bhīmasenāya saṃyuge tomarān prāhiṇoc chīghraṃ caturdaśa śilāśitān
english: Then the Kaliṅga king, enraged, swiftly hurled at Bhīmasena in the encounter fourteen lances whetted upon stone.

sanskrit: tān aprāptān mahābāhuḥ khagatān eva pāṇḍavaḥ ciccheda sahasā rājann asaṃbhrānto varāsinā
english: Before they reached him, while they were still in the air, the mighty-armed Pāṇḍava cut them apart at once, O king, unflustered, with his excellent sword.

sanskrit: nikṛtya tu raṇe bhīmas tomarān vai caturdaśa bhānumantam abhiprekṣya prādravat puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: Having shorn through those fourteen lances in the battle, Bhīma, that bull among men, fixed his gaze upon Bhānumat and rushed at him.

sanskrit: bhānumāṃs tu tato bhīmaṃ śaravarṣeṇa chādayan nanāda balavan nādaṃ nādayāno nabhastalam
english: But Bhānumat then, covering Bhīma with a shower of arrows, raised a mighty roar, making the vault of heaven resound.

sanskrit: na taṃ sa mamṛṣe bhīmaḥ siṃhanādaṃ mahāraṇe tataḥ svareṇa mahatā vinanāda mahāsvanam
english: Bhīma did not endure that lion's roar in the great battle, and so he too bellowed forth a loud cry with a mighty voice.

sanskrit: tena śabdena vitrastā kaliṅgānāṃ varūthinī na bhīmaṃ samare mene mānuṣaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Terrified by that sound, the army of the Kaliṅgas, O bull of the Bharatas, no longer reckoned Bhīma in the fight to be a man.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahārāja naditvā vipulaṃ svanam sāsir vegād avaplutya dantābhyāṃ vāraṇottamam
english: Then Bhīma, O great king, having roared a vast cry, sword in hand, leapt swiftly and, by its two tusks, seized that finest of elephants.

sanskrit: āruroha tato madhyaṃ nāgarājasya māriṣa khaḍgena pṛthunā madhye bhānumantam athācchinat
english: Then he mounted upon the middle of that king of elephants, O sire, and with his broad sword cut Bhānumat asunder through the middle.

sanskrit: so 'ntarāyudhinaṃ hatvā rājaputram ariṃdamaḥ gurubhārasahaskandhe nāgasyāsim apātayat
english: Having slain the prince fighting close beside him, that subduer of foes brought down his sword upon the elephant's shoulder, which could bear a heavy load.

sanskrit: chinnaskandhaḥ sa vinadan papāta gajayūthapaḥ ārugṇaḥ sindhuvegena sānumān iva parvataḥ
english: With its shoulder cleft, that lord of the elephant herd, crying out, fell, like a crag-crested mountain washed away by the rush of a river.

sanskrit: tatas tasmād avaplutya gajād bhārata bhārataḥ khaḍgapāṇir adīnātmā atiṣṭhad bhuvi daṃśitaḥ
english: Then, O Bhārata, the descendant of Bharata, leaping down from that elephant, sword in hand, undaunted in spirit, stood mailed upon the ground.

sanskrit: sa cacāra bahūn mārgān abhītaḥ pātayan gajān agnicakram ivāviddhaṃ sarvataḥ pratyadṛśyata
english: He ranged along many paths, fearless, felling elephants, and appeared on every side like a whirling wheel of fire.

sanskrit: aśvavṛndeṣu nāgeṣu rathānīkeṣu cābhibhūḥ padātīnāṃ ca saṃgheṣu vinighnañ śoṇitokṣitaḥ śyenavad vyacarad bhīmo raṇe ripubalotkaṭaḥ
english: Overpowering them, smiting down troops of horses, elephants, ranks of cars, and bands of foot-soldiers, drenched in blood, Bhīma ranged like a hawk through the battle, terrible amid the host of his foes.

sanskrit: chindaṃs teṣāṃ śarīrāṇi śirāṃsi ca mahājavaḥ khaḍgena śitadhāreṇa saṃyuge gajayodhinām
english: Swift as he was, he severed the bodies and the heads of those elephant-warriors in the encounter with his keen-edged sword.

sanskrit: padātir ekaḥ saṃkruddhaḥ śatrūṇāṃ bhayavardhanaḥ mohayām āsa ca tadā kālāntakayamopamaḥ
english: A single foot-soldier, enraged, swelling the terror of his foes, he bewildered them then, like Yama, the ender, at the time of doom.

sanskrit: mūḍhāś ca te tam evājau vinadantaḥ samādravan sāsim uttamavegena vicarantaṃ mahāraṇe
english: And those bewildered men, roaring, rushed upon him in the battle, as he ranged with utmost speed, sword in hand, through the great fray.

sanskrit: nikṛtya rathinām ājau ratheṣāś ca yugāni ca jaghāna rathinaś cāpi balavān arimardanaḥ
english: Cutting through the car-poles and yokes of the car-warriors in the battle, that mighty crusher of foes slew the car-warriors as well.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaś caran mārgān subahūn pratyadṛśyata bhrāntam udbhrāntam āviddham āplutaṃ prasṛtaṃ sṛtam saṃpātaṃ samudīryaṃ ca darśayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Bhīmasena, ranging along very many paths, was seen everywhere; the Pāṇḍava displayed the wheeling, the upward whirling, the brandishing, the leaping, the springing forth, the gliding, the onset and the upward thrust.

sanskrit: ke cid agrāsinā chinnāḥ pāṇḍavena mahātmanā vinedur bhinnamarmāṇo nipetuś ca gatāsavaḥ
english: Some, cleft by the point of the sword of the high-souled Pāṇḍava, cried out, their vitals pierced, and fell down lifeless.

sanskrit: chinnadantāgrahastāś ca bhinnakumbhās tathāpare viyodhāḥ svāny anīkāni jaghnur bhārata vāraṇāḥ nipetur urvyāṃ ca tathā vinadanto mahāravān
english: And some elephants, their tusk-tips and trunks lopped off, their frontal lobes shattered, riderless, smote their own ranks, O Bhārata, and fell upon the earth, bellowing great cries.

sanskrit: chinnāṃś ca tomarāṃś cāpān mahāmātraśirāṃsi ca paristomāni citrāṇi kakṣyāś ca kanakojjvalāḥ
english: And severed lances and bows and the heads of elephant-drivers, gay-colored housings and girths gleaming with gold,

sanskrit: graiveyāṇy atha śaktīś ca patākāḥ kaṇapāṃs tathā tūṇīrāṇy atha yantrāṇi vicitrāṇi dhanūṃṣi ca
english: and neck-ornaments and spears, banners and barbed darts, quivers and engines and many-hued bows,

sanskrit: agnikuṇḍāni śubhrāṇi tottrāṃś caivāṅkuśaiḥ saha ghaṇṭāś ca vividhā rājan hemagarbhāṃs tsarūn api patataḥ patitāṃś caiva paśyāmaḥ saha sādibhiḥ
english: and bright fire-pots, and goads together with elephant-hooks, and bells of many kinds, O king, and gold-cored sword-hilts, falling and fallen, together with their riders — all these we saw.

sanskrit: chinnagātrāvarakarair nihataiś cāpi vāraṇaiḥ āsīt tasmin samāstīrṇā patitair bhūr nagair iva
english: With elephants slain, their limb-guards and trunks shorn away, the earth in that place was strewn over with the fallen, as though with mountains.

sanskrit: vimṛdyaivaṃ mahānāgān mamardāśvān nararṣabhaḥ aśvārohavarāṃś cāpi pātayām āsa bhārata tad ghoram abhavad yuddhaṃ tasya teṣāṃ ca bhārata
english: Having thus crushed those great elephants, that bull among men trampled the horses and struck down the finest of the horsemen, O Bhārata; and dreadful was that battle between him and them, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: khalīnāny atha yoktrāṇi kaśāś ca kanakojjvalāḥ paristomāś ca prāsāś ca ṛṣṭayaś ca mahādhanāḥ
english: And bits and harness-straps and whips gleaming with gold, and housings and javelins and costly swords,

sanskrit: kavacāny atha carmāṇi citrāṇy āstaraṇāni ca tatra tatrāpaviddhāni vyadṛśyanta mahāhave
english: and corselets and shields and gaily-colored saddle-cloths, scattered here and there, were seen in that great battle.

sanskrit: prothayantrair vicitraiś ca śastraiś ca vimalais tathā sa cakre vasudhāṃ kīrṇāṃ śabalaiḥ kusumair iva
english: With manifold horse-trappings and with bright weapons he made the earth bestrewn, as though with many-colored flowers.

sanskrit: āplutya rathinaḥ kāṃś cit parāmṛśya mahābalaḥ pātayām āsa khaḍgena sadhvajān api pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Leaping upon and seizing certain car-warriors, the mighty Pāṇḍava struck them down with his sword, banners and all.

sanskrit: muhur utpatato dikṣu dhāvataś ca yaśasvinaḥ mārgāṃś ca carataś citrān vyasmayanta raṇe janāḥ
english: As that glorious one again and again sprang up in all directions, and ran, and ranged along wondrous paths, the people in the battle marveled.

sanskrit: nijaghāna padā kāṃś cid ākṣipyānyān apothayat khaḍgenānyāṃś ca ciccheda nādenānyāṃś ca bhīṣayan
english: Some he slew with his foot; others he seized and dashed to the ground; others he cut down with his sword; and yet others he terrified with his roar.

sanskrit: ūruvegena cāpy anyān pātayām āsa bhūtale apare cainam ālokya bhayāt pañcatvam āgatāḥ
english: Others again he felled to the ground by the force of his thighs; and some, merely beholding him, in their terror passed into death.

sanskrit: evaṃ sā bahulā senā kaliṅgānāṃ tarasvinām parivārya raṇe bhīṣmaṃ bhīmasenam upādravat
english: Thus that numerous army of the swift Kaliṅgas, having ringed Bhīṣma about in the battle, rushed upon Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tataḥ kaliṅgasainyānāṃ pramukhe bharatarṣabha śrutāyuṣam abhiprekṣya bhīmasenaḥ samabhyayāt
english: Then, O bull of the Bharatas, fixing his gaze upon Śrutāyus at the head of the Kaliṅga host, Bhīmasena advanced against him.

sanskrit: tam āyāntam abhiprekṣya kaliṅgo navabhiḥ śaraiḥ bhīmasenam ameyātmā pratyavidhyat stanāntare
english: Seeing him coming on, the Kaliṅga king of immeasurable spirit pierced Bhīmasena in the breast with nine arrows.

sanskrit: kaliṅgabāṇābhihatas tottrārdita iva dvipaḥ bhīmasenaḥ prajajvāla krodhenāgnir ivendhanaiḥ
english: Struck by the Kaliṅga's arrows, like an elephant tormented by the goad, Bhīmasena blazed up with wrath, as fire blazes with fuel.

sanskrit: athāśokaḥ samādāya rathaṃ hemapariṣkṛtam bhīmaṃ saṃpādayām āsa rathena rathasārathiḥ
english: Then Aśoka, bringing up a car adorned with gold, the charioteer furnished Bhīma with that car.

sanskrit: tam āruhya rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ kaunteyaḥ śatrusūdanaḥ kaliṅgam abhidudrāva tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Swiftly mounting that car, the son of Kuntī, slayer of foes, rushed upon the Kaliṅga king, crying, 'Stand! Stand!'

sanskrit: tataḥ śrutāyur balavān bhīmāya niśitāñ śarān preṣayām āsa saṃkruddho darśayan pāṇilāghavam
english: Then mighty Śrutāyus, enraged, sent forth sharp arrows at Bhīma, displaying the lightness of his hand.

sanskrit: sa kārmukavarotsṛṣṭair navabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ samāhato bhṛśaṃ rājan kaliṅgena mahāyaśāḥ saṃcukrudhe bhṛśaṃ bhīmo daṇḍāhata ivoragaḥ
english: Sorely struck by nine sharp arrows loosed from that excellent bow by the Kaliṅga king, O king, the glorious Bhīma grew exceedingly wrathful, like a serpent beaten with a staff.

sanskrit: kruddhaś ca cāpam āyamya balavad balināṃ varaḥ kaliṅgam avadhīt pārtho bhīmaḥ saptabhir āyasaiḥ
english: And enraged, that best of the mighty, the son of Pṛthā, Bhīma, drawing his bow with force, slew the Kaliṅga king with seven iron shafts.

sanskrit: kṣurābhyāṃ cakrarakṣau ca kaliṅgasya mahābalau satyadevaṃ ca satyaṃ ca prāhiṇod yamasādanam
english: And with two razor-edged arrows he dispatched to the abode of Yama the two mighty wheel-guards of the Kaliṅga king, Satyadeva and Satya.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar ameyātmā nārācair niśitais tribhiḥ ketumantaṃ raṇe bhīmo 'gamayad yamasādanam
english: Then again, Bhīma of immeasurable spirit, with three sharp iron arrows, sent Ketumat in the battle to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: tataḥ kaliṅgāḥ saṃkruddhā bhīmasenam amarṣaṇam anīkair bahusāhasraiḥ kṣatriyāḥ samavārayan
english: Then the Kaliṅgas, enraged, the warriors hemmed in the impatient Bhīmasena with many thousands of troops.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaktigadākhaḍgatomararṣṭiparaśvadhaiḥ kaliṅgāś ca tato rājan bhīmasenam avākiran
english: Then with spears and maces and swords, with lances and javelins and battle-axes, the Kaliṅgas, O king, overwhelmed Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: saṃnivārya sa tāṃ ghorāṃ śaravṛṣṭiṃ samutthitām gadām ādāya tarasā pariplutya mahābalaḥ bhīmaḥ saptaśatān vīrān anayad yamasādanam
english: Warding off that terrible shower of arrows that had risen against him, the mighty Bhīma, taking up his mace and swiftly leaping forth, led seven hundred heroes to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: punaś caiva dvisāhasrān kaliṅgān arimardanaḥ prāhiṇon mṛtyulokāya tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: And once more that crusher of foes sent two thousand Kaliṅgas to the world of death; and that was as though a marvel.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa tāny anīkāni kaliṅgānāṃ punaḥ punaḥ bibheda samare vīraḥ prekṣya bhīṣmaṃ mahāvratam
english: Thus again and again the hero shattered those ranks of the Kaliṅgas in the battle, with his gaze upon Bhīṣma of the great vow.

sanskrit: hatārohāś ca mātaṅgāḥ pāṇḍavena mahātmanā viprajagmur anīkeṣu meghā vātahatā iva mṛdnantaḥ svāny anīkāni vinadantaḥ śarāturāḥ
english: And the elephants, their riders slain by the high-souled Pāṇḍava, scattered through the ranks like clouds driven by the wind, trampling their own troops and bellowing, sore wounded by arrows.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhaṃ prādhmāpayad balī sarvakāliṅgasainyānāṃ manāṃsi samakampayat
english: Then the mighty-armed Bhīma, that strong one, blew his conch and made the hearts of all the Kāliṅga soldiery tremble.

sanskrit: mohaś cāpi kaliṅgānām āviveśa paraṃtapa prākampanta ca sainyāni vāhanāni ca sarvaśaḥ
english: And a stupor seized upon the Kaliṅgas, O scorcher of foes, and their soldiers and their mounts trembled in every part.

sanskrit: bhīmena samare rājan gajendreṇeva sarvataḥ mārgān bahūn vicaratā dhāvatā ca tatas tataḥ muhur utpatatā caiva saṃmohaḥ samajāyata
english: By Bhīma in the battle, O king, ranging on every side like a lordly elephant along many paths, running here and there, again and again springing up, a bewilderment was wrought among them.

sanskrit: bhīmasenabhayatrastaṃ sainyaṃ ca samakampata kṣobhyamāṇam asaṃbādhaṃ grāheṇeva mahat saraḥ
english: And the host, panic-stricken with fear of Bhīmasena, quivered, churned and broken open, like a great lake stirred by a crocodile.

sanskrit: trāsiteṣu ca vīreṣu bhīmenādbhutakarmaṇā punarāvartamāneṣu vidravatsu ca saṃghaśaḥ
english: When the heroes had been terrified by Bhīma of wondrous deeds, some rallying back and some fleeing away in companies,

sanskrit: sarvakāliṅgayodheṣu pāṇḍūnāṃ dhvajinīpatiḥ abravīt svāny anīkāni yudhyadhvam iti pārṣataḥ
english: while all the Kāliṅga warriors were thus, the commander of the Pāṇḍava host, the son of Pṛṣata, said to his own ranks, 'Fight!'

sanskrit: senāpativacaḥ śrutvā śikhaṇḍipramukhā gaṇāḥ bhīmam evābhyavartanta rathānīkaiḥ prahāribhiḥ
english: Hearing the words of their commander, the troops led by Śikhaṇḍin advanced toward Bhīma with their smiting bands of cars.

sanskrit: dharmarājaś ca tān sarvān upajagrāha pāṇḍavaḥ mahatā meghavarṇena nāgānīkena pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: And the Pāṇḍava, the King of Righteousness, supported them all from behind with a great cloud-colored division of elephants.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃcodya sarvāṇi svāny anīkāni pārṣataḥ bhīmasenasya jagrāha pārṣṇiṃ satpuruṣocitām
english: Having thus urged on all his own ranks, the son of Pṛṣata took up the guarding of Bhīmasena's rear, as befits a good man.

sanskrit: na hi pāñcālarājasya loke kaś cana vidyate bhīmasātyakayor anyaḥ prāṇebhyaḥ priyakṛttamaḥ
english: For in the world there was none other for the king of the Pāñcālas, save Bhīma and Sātyaki, dearer than his own life's breath.

sanskrit: so 'paśyat taṃ kaliṅgeṣu carantam arisūdanam bhīmasenaṃ mahābāhuṃ pārṣataḥ paravīrahā
english: The son of Pṛṣata, slayer of hostile heroes, beheld that slayer of foes, the mighty-armed Bhīmasena, ranging among the Kaliṅgas.

sanskrit: nanarda bahudhā rājan hṛṣṭaś cāsīt paraṃtapaḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau ca samare siṃhanādaṃ nanāda ca
english: He roared again and again, O king, and was filled with joy, that scorcher of foes; and in the battle he blew his conch and gave forth a lion's roar.

sanskrit: sa ca pārāvatāśvasya rathe hemapariṣkṛte kovidāradhvajaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenaḥ samāśvasat
english: And Bhīmasena, beholding upon the gold-adorned car of him whose horses were dove-gray the banner of the kovidāra tree, took heart again.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā kaliṅgaiḥ samabhidrutam bhīmasenam ameyātmā trāṇāyājau samabhyayāt
english: But Dhṛṣṭadyumna of immeasurable spirit, seeing Bhīmasena beset by the Kaliṅgas, advanced in the battle to his rescue.

sanskrit: tau dūrāt sātyakir dṛṣṭvā dhṛṣṭadyumnavṛkodarau kaliṅgān samare vīrau yodhayantau manasvinau
english: Sātyaki, seeing from afar those two, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Vṛkodara, the high-minded heroes giving battle to the Kaliṅgas in the fray,

sanskrit: sa tatra gatvā śaineyo javena jayatāṃ varaḥ pārthapārṣatayoḥ pārṣṇiṃ jagrāha puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: the grandson of Śini, that best of victors, having sped thither swiftly, that bull among men, took up the guarding of the rear of the son of Pṛthā and the son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā kadanaṃ tatra pragṛhītaśarāsanaḥ āsthito raudram ātmānaṃ jaghāna samare parān
english: There, working havoc, his bow taken up, abiding in a terrible mood, he slew his foes in the battle.

sanskrit: kaliṅgaprabhavāṃ caiva māṃsaśoṇitakardamām rudhirasyandinīṃ tatra bhīmaḥ prāvartayan nadīm
english: And there Bhīma set flowing a river, sprung from the Kaliṅgas, miry with flesh and blood, streaming with gore.

sanskrit: antareṇa kaliṅgānāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca vāhinīm saṃtatāra sudustārāṃ bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ
english: Between the host of the Kaliṅgas and that of the Pāṇḍavas, the mighty Bhīmasena crossed over that river most hard to cross.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā prākrośaṃs tāvakā nṛpa kālo 'yaṃ bhīmarūpeṇa kaliṅgaiḥ saha yudhyate
english: Seeing Bhīmasena thus, O king, your men cried out, 'This is Death himself, in the form of Bhīma, doing battle with the Kaliṅgas!'

sanskrit: tataḥ śāṃtanavo bhīṣmaḥ śrutvā taṃ ninadaṃ raṇe abhyayāt tvarito bhīmaṃ vyūḍhānīkaḥ samantataḥ
english: Then Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu, hearing that uproar in the battle, made haste against Bhīma, his ranks arrayed on every side.
